While I respect the opinion of everybody who has posted before me I myself can't agree with a lot of the statements made here.

- We already have a singler-player medipack that can be purchased in-game. It would be nice to see a team medipack/ammobox that could be placed on the field for all (allied) players to use.

- I don't really like the idea of having a way to change weapons or items mid-game. I feel it would unhinge the balance of the fight and give an advantage to the players with the most availible out-of-game resources such as General Points or Tokens.

- The option to change some of the settings mid-game might be nice, but is not really needed. As long as a player remembers to adjust the game settings to their liking before a match begins there is little to worry about.

That said, there are a few small things of my own I would like to see changed.

- The price of tokens decreased. I would like to at least get 5,000 tokens (as opposed ot the regular 2,000) for $9.99, 10,000 tokens for $19.99, etc. Increasing/rounding these numbers may make players more likely to buy tokens as they would be getting more for their money. Companies like Nexon (a terrible company) who give 10,000 NX for $10.00 (bearing in mind that NX is their premium currency and the prices here are American) seemingly give a better deal. I do want to remind everybody reading this however that Nexon's premium items are much more expensive for similar durations, and just a small boost (as mentioned earlier) on Infernum's part would make them the better buy.

- I would like to see the explosives count increased from 1 to 2 tosses. I am aware the smoke bomb gives three tosses, but I feel that three tosses of any bomb (without buying an ammo increase) is to many while having one toss seems to be a bit lacking. I would also like to see some remote-controled epxlosives (claymores/mines, maybe a B-4 Plastique Explosive) made availible in game.

I'd love to see bomboy2121's idea of a team medipack/ammobox implimented along with the price changes and the modification of the explosive's count. Hopefully these will be changes Infernum will consider. I'm sure many other players would love to see the above and other impliments implimented. Until then, happy gaming and posting.

For those who are new to the Brick-Force community,

Welcome!

Here's some tips to get you started when playing in Shooter mode.
(Note that I won't be saying much about ideal weapons. Everyone has his/her own weapon that he's/ she's good with.)

Tip 1: Use The Shift key.

The Shift key causes your character to slow down, but slowly hip-fire aim better.
Your cross-hair won't spread that much, the Shift key causes to recoil to drop down a bit.

Tip 2: Avoiding Hits

When your being shot at, if theres no potential cover, you'll have to rely on the w-a-s-d keys,
as in every First Person Shooter, W is forwards, A is Left, D is right, and S is backwards.
Now here comes the "dodge" trick.

When your being shot at, instantly jump to the left or right to surprise the shooter, also don't forget to shoot him/her too.

But what if you ran outta' ammo?

Well what do you think your pistol is for?

Get your pistol, and shoot at that player!

Tip 3: The "melee/nade sprint".

As you know, there isn't actually a sprinting option, nor key for sprinting.
However there is an action panel item for going fast.
...but what if you used it all up?

No worries, although not as fast. It's as efficient.

Holding (not using) a grenade, or your melee weapon will make you go faster.

If I have to sum it up with a graph, (Red= Slow, Yellow-Mid speed, Green-Fast)

Primary
Secondary
Melee
Grenade

Now, if you aren't a rich guy who has oooooh-so much money, (which we all are.)
You'll have to rely on your general points.

Now getting clothes and all for fashion and more points and XP may be nice.
But it just is.

...Well...you don't really have too.

Check your balance, and time left to stop playing.

When you get an item, lets say for one day. It's 720 points, for example.

Or you got a whole Freaking bunch. And it's total is 3000+ points,
lets say you need to earn more then that from matches in order to balance, or increase your economy.

For some of you, yes, it's annoying.

...but that's economy for ya'...

Before buying, just think. Will I need it? Can I do without it in this match? Will I have enough time?
...and such. But.

This tip is kinda important. So many people don't seem to realize this and throw away their spawn protection when they don't even have a good shot.

It's also easy to exploit when you're patrolling (or literally camping) their spawn. Get yourself a place where you can quickly dart in and out of cover (like a corner, or a wall that you can jump up on). Wait for them to spot you, then take cover after a bit. If you timed it right, they'll start shooting at your cover without hitting you, thereby forfeiting their spawn protection. If they keep spraying however, wait until you hear them reload, then rush 'em.

It's all about practice, really.

- People are jumping around "being monkeys" because stationary targets are mostly easy picks (I admit, I have derped on a few occasions and wasted a whole mag on a person standing still ). This is something you just have to learn by doing it repeatedly; Whenever you see a moving target, try to shoot it. Eventually you'll get the hang of it, and you'll be able to shoot even those who are doing really random evasion maneuvers.

- Sniping on a high level in this game requires really, REALLY twitchy reflexes. See target -> react -> scope -> aim -> shoot, all that in a second or so when talking about really high-level snipers. Again, learning by doing, there's nothing else to say about it. Edit: As Holdonjohn mentioned, the order of the points 'scope' and 'aim' in the chain of actions is interchangeable, depending on play style, and I use a little bit of both. I just wrote down one of the chains to avoid redundancy :P

- Learn to shoot while moving/jumping. Being able to attack while evading enemy bullets = thumbs up.

Just a few quick pointers, if someone likes to point out something which isn't all about practice, feel free to do so.

The actual sens depends of what mouse speed you have on your PC in general, what mouse you use and what mouse pad/table you have. Like, my sens could be as fast as Awmnawm's sens, even though his appears faster. Just wanna' make sure that everybody is aware of this, so they don't try to change it to someone elses sens, in the belief that it might be more suitable for them.

Anyways, I currently use sens 10, it seems pretty well-rounded for any weapon I pick at the moment.

A good tip I got back in my Counter-Strike 1.3 days (when I was actually good at FPS games) to find a good sensivity for the intermediate+ gamer; is that, if you grib your mouse, and make a left to the right movement with your hand that feels comfortable for you, then you should set your sens on your mouse, so you have turned 180 degrees (looking the opposite direction) when you make that movement. Then you only have to lift your mouse and do it again to look in the first direction. In this way, you can get really fast reactions and a steady aim at the same time, with just a bit practise and keep the same sensivity in all games, so you don't lose skills when you try out a new game, but actually end up adding to your general amount of skills. I hope that made just some sense.

My opinions on your suggestions;

"Crawling-To Crawl Through Small Or Tight Spaces For Example:Vents In Buildings"
This one I like. However, that would also mean that a ton of maps would have to be re-adjusted for this, so people who have already made maps would probably not like it due to the cost of editing maps being ludicrous.

"New Controls-Up Key:Get Up From Crouching,Down Key:Crouch,Left And Right Keys:Barrel Roll"
Most people don't have three hands, and since the left hand is used for WASD and the right one for the mouse (assuming you're a right-handed person), this would get really unergonomic. Also, just nitpicking, barrel roll is an aerial-only term.

"Picking Up-So You Can Pick Up Guns Or Ammo And Use It"
Yes, please.

"Useable Transportation-Using Cars To Get Faster To Other Placlashes And Run Over People With Them"
No. If they were fast enough to run someone over with, they have no place in this game, seeing how slow the movement speed of the brick-men is.

"Making Cars-Make Seats,Wheels,Steering Wheels,Doors,And Bright Lights To Make A Car And Drive It"
See the point above.

"Knifes-As Melee Weapons"
Sure, why not. As for them making more damage, no.

"Training-Making Training Arenas And Training With Weapons"
Elaborate, please.

"Testing-Testing Weapons Before Buying Them"
On a target range-type of map, this would probably be pointless. Getting to test the weapons in a real match? Maybe, if the trial was limited to one game/gun, or something.

"Grapple Hooks/Guns-Get Somewhere Faster"
This would take a ridiculous amount of time to implement and get balanced. If it would be for sale in the shop, the grappling hook would give a game-breaking advantage. If it would be made available for all, a lot of matches would become a huge cluster-*expletive*.

"Flashlights-To See In Dark Places"
There are no places dark enough to require a flashlight in Brick-Force, and neither should there be. No.

"Doors-To Get In Other Rooms"
Besides some TF2-style spawn point doors, no thanks.

The ones I haven't commented on are things that I don't have anything to say about.

title: A beginner's guide to clothing and accessories.

posts.h:
Okay, I know the update only recently came out, but it surprises me too see that not a lot of people are taking advantage of the new clothing and accessory system. There has been some debate that upgraded weapons provide a big advantage, but killing your opponent almost twice as fast isn't necessarily going to benefit you as much as taking three times the bullets.

Onward to the Wall O' Text!

So first off, lets start with the basics. What are clothing and accessories? What do they do?

Clothing is something you can customize your Brickforce character with. You can buy them from the item shop. You can buy them for a certain amount of time with force points or permanently with tokens if you really wish to do so. You start off with an army jacket and army pants, which are indeed permanent, but they are useless because they are never capable of providing you a boost. Most of the clothing and accessories you buy don't give any additional effects when you first get them. They have to be upgraded first to be of any real use to you. Some accessories do give out additional max ammo, max grenades, and max luck though.

How do upgrade my clothing and/or accessories once I‘ve bought them?

To upgrade your recently bought sparkly new gear you need some equipment gems. They come in four sizes. Small equipment gems, medium equipment gems, large equipment gems, and elite equipment gems. Medium and large equipment gems both require you to be at a high rank to use them, so for the sake of argument I'll presume you aren't at that high of a rank. Elite equipment gems and small equipment gems can be used regardless of your in-game rank. You can only buy elite gems with tokens though. And as for small equipment gems, they can only upgrade a stat on your equipment three times. Now don't be confused. They can upgrade your clothing and accessories more than three times, but not any individual stat above three times.

So you got your gems, not go into your items and go to the clothes or accessories section. You are going to have to use that armour in order to be able to upgrade it. If it's not yet in use just double click on the piece of gear and it should ask you if you wish to use it. Now click the piece of equipment and you should see four icons at the bottom of the screen.



The first is the "Clear Expired Items" button. The second is the "Unequip All" button. The third is the "Item Upgrade" button, the one we are looking for. The fourth one is the "Merge" button. I'll talk about the importance of that feature later.

So now just select your gem and you are off.

What are some of the benefits for upgrading my clothing and accessories?

What you will get from upgrading and the strength of the benefiting quality in question depends on what you are upgrading. For example, a helmet. When upgrading any helmet you can either get 2 armour from the upgrade, or 1% increase to your luck. Since a beginner can upgrade a helmet's armour three times, he can get 6 armour from his helmet alone and 3% luck. The jacket and pants both have possible upgrades of armour, increased xp, and increased fp(force points). You only get 0.5% xp/fp for each upgrade in that department. Clothing has the benefit of giving more armour with each upgrade over accessories. However the xp and fp modifiers remain the same.

So what that means is a jacket upgraded to the max in all departments will give you 20 armour, 5% xp bonus, and 5% fp bonus. Any accessory upgraded to the max will give you 10 armour, 5% xp bonus, and 5% fp bonus. One thing to note though. When upgrading with small, medium, or large gems you will often find the armour stat upgrades over the other available options. It means you are less likely to increase your luck from upgrading your helmet over your armour. Same goes with xp and fp modifiers, you are more likely to upgrade armour over everything else when using a gem that upgrades one stat randomly.

-continuing on to the next post-
posts.t: A beginner's guide to clothing and accessories.

posts.h:
-continued-

Armour huh, why do I need it exactly? What does it do?

Armour is kinda like increased health. It is essential against sniper users and helps give you a competitive edge against other players. If my calculations are correct. You can max out your armour at 140. 42 if you only have access to small gems. 84 if you have access to medium gems. What does this mean though? Is it like I have (100)hp + (140)armour = (240)hp ? Well, yes. It doesn’t exactly act like hp though. Someone with 140 armour is essentially like someone with 240hp, but armour can only take about 66% of the damage of a shot. That means if someone does shot that would normally take away 30 hp to you, 20 damage is done to your armour and 10 to your hp.

If the sniper rifle is upgraded, you would need more armour just to keep breathing though. I think currently for every upgrade to damage on a one hit kill sniper you will need 3 armour just to cancel it out. So a BWM normally takes away 100 hp. A BWM upgraded to the max will take away 130.

You can still probably be killed in one blow if the sniper user is good enough to get a brick shot and your armour is low enough. However it is likely if you have enough armour even a brickshot from a BWM (the only current one hit kill sniper in the game) will not kill you. Brickshots don't even seem to do 1.5 damage anymore, where as they used to do 5x the damage.

Okay, I can see the benefits, but do I really want to waste 30,000 force points for a months of 42 armour?

Well, this brings me back to the wonderful merge option. A lot of people here would hesitate spending so many force points on something that will expire in a month. They would probably only upgrade their permanent armour, if they had any. But thanks to the wonderful merge option you don’t have to worry about spending points all for not. Yes, that’s right. You upgraded your equipment and it’s about to expire? Just buy another set and merge it to keep all those wonderful upgrades you paid for. You could buy a year’s worth of time on all your clothing and accessories if you so desired. Considering how cheap clothing is, buying more time for your set shouldn’t be too much of a problem.

Now the 30k of force points is just an estimate on my part. With that many points you should be able to buy yourself a full set(including each kind of accessory) for an entire month and deck it out with the max armour possible using small gems and even get a 10% xp and fp boost too boot. Yep, 30k for 42 armour and a 10% xp/fp boost. Seems like a good deal eh?

Merging means I‘ve have to pay to keep my armour since it isn‘t permanent?

Well, yes and no. If you invested 30k into a nice spiffy set or clothing and accessories you should have at least a 10% bonus to fp, if not 15% even. What this means is the armour should pay for itself if you play enough. You have to play quite a bit though for it to pay for itself fully though. Depending on what look you went with, your armour will cost a bit more to renew each month. My estimates are if you like to go flashy with the best set(in terms of price I mean) available it will cost you 15k fp a month. Now the more expensive clothing doesn’t actually do anything better. So you can go with the cheaper (and in my opinion uglier) clothing if you want to save 5k of points in a month.

So this bonus fp may not seem like a lot, but with repairing(aka, gun tax) taking up a lot of your profits it means this 10%-15% of your earns is more than it seems. You will need to earn about 100k of fp a month in order to pay for the armour with the profits alone. But considering the 100k of fp will be ransacked down to 80k or less (from all that repairing) you might be happy to suddenly have that extra 10-15k paying for your armour free of charge. And the boosted xp will help you achieve the higher ranks easier so you can eventually use those higher tier gems if tokens aren’t your sort of thing.

Golden Beta Helm?
So if you played in the closed beta, you got one of these bad boys. Now why do I bring it up? Well, it’s a permanent piece of clothing that can be upgraded and it can save you some dough because of it. That means you will never have to re-buy some clothing to merge with it each month. It should save you 1000-1500 points a month. So if you have this piece make sure to upgrade it, upgrade it as much as you can. Helmets are the only piece of equipment that can give out luck through upgrading too, and it gives out a healthy 2 armour each upgrade, which doesn’t hurt.

-yep, still more-

-last post, I swear-

Tokens galore, the advantages of token buying?

If the upkeep of buying clothing each month is too much of a burden for you or you just want some really awesome threads in terms of stats, you can go with the alternative. Tokens! Yes, you can buy a piece of clothing permanently with tokens. It will cost you quite a bit though, but you don’t have to worry about those upkeep costs for your clothing. It will cost you about 12000 tokens(30$ give or take) (10500 if you have a golden beta helm) for a full permanent set of clothing and accessories. To upgrade these things to max though with some elite equipments gems will cost you quite a bit. My estimates are at about 20000 tokens if you want a full set of armour upgraded to the max. That’s about 50 bucks of tokens.

The benefits of the elite equipment gems though? 140 armour permanently (meaning you are nearly a god in battle), 50% increase to fp and xp during a match, and 10% luck(very nice against sniper shots when it actually works), and no more worrying about how long your clothing and accessories will last if you went with a permanent clothing set.

Some debate whether buying permanent clothing and accessories with tokens is unfair or not?

Well, for those of you who think it is unfair to offer the permanent clothing for tokens only, consider this. People have to pay 30 dollars worth of tokens if not more. And for what? That’s not even a competitive in-game advantage they are buying. Anyone can buy clothing. The only thing they are buying is the ability to not have to pay 10k of fp a month for their set anymore.

That pretty much raps up everything I can think of about clothing, armour, accessories, and the like. If you got some input, something you think I missed, or if I'm off about something feel free to tell me. I don't mind harsh criticism. And sorry about the triple post. The forums only allow 5000 characters per post.
Wonderful guide, should be great for everyone, especially since the gem update. Bravo.

title: Tips on Shooter mode for newcomers!

posts.h:
Brick-Force, Intro to Shooter mode.

Play on any map, mode, with any your friends, against or alongside each other in this FPS
(First Person Shooter)

Maps with several different styles.
Many weapons.
And many classic game-modes such as Deathmatch or Capture the Flag (CTF)!

To get you started into shooter mode, here is some tips and stuff, that would help you and advise you in-game.

::CONTENTS::

Chapter One: Shooting

Chapter Two: Avoiding Shots

Chapter Three: Stealth

Chapter Four: Side Tips

Chapter Five: Economy

Chapter Six: Movement


:Other Guides:

-20 Tips to Make You a Better Gamer by SiNNiR

-Weapon Repair FAQ by EhseJaybie


-A beginner's guide to clothing and accessories by BK201


-List of in-game ranks by lunboks


► ⚠ Brick-Force Guides


More Intermediate Tips will be added! Time for your advice!
posts.t: Tips on Shooter mode for newcomers!

posts.h:
::CHAPTER ONE: SHOOTING::

Tip 1: Aim

Brick-Force throws you into the classic FPS gameplay, you, your eyes, and your gun.
Note that you can't aim with guns except with Sniper Rifles.

Meaning that it would be seem you're Hip-Firing. (Shooting without aiming steady.)

When shooting, your cross-hair will jump and expand (Due to recoil). in all FPS's, the bigger the cross-hair,
the lesser accuracy.

Accuracy really effects your aim, no mater how powerful your aim is.
No aim, no power.

Now to get to the point, how can I "aim" better in Brick-Force?

Not so hard. Just press the SHIFT key while shooting.
This will reduce about half of the recoil, and gain you a much better accuracy. Just aim the target after that.



However, note that using the SHIFT key shall reduce your speed. It will also cause you to make no sound while walking.



Tip 2: Aim for the Brain

Headshots, or known as "BrickShots" in Brick-Force, kills the foe in one hit (Well Multiplies damage given.), regardless of weapon.
However, BrickShots kills aren't obtained by luck.



Aim for the Brain, between the eyebrows while shooting. Regardless of position, you can also hit the side-middle or top-middle of the head to earn one.

So aiming for the head, means more damage!

Tip 3: Shooting Enemies

Shooting may be nice, but at times, you must choose your targets, one by one.

If an enemy is right next to you, and, well, trying to shoot you.
Don't aim at another enemy. Take Him/Her down first, then resume shooter.

Tip 4: Stance

When you stop to shoot, check where you are.

What is the place around you like? A " T "? A Line/Path? Or an openly wide area?
When your moving around shooting, be aware of where enemies may pop up to surprise you.

Note that in T shaped roads, don't stand in the middle of it. Although you might want to go forward, you have to be careful for your sides.
As for open areas, try to find the best cover for yourself.


Tip 5: About Reloading

When your mag (Cartridge containing bullets for the gun.) runs out of ammo, you know you need to reload.
However there are times to and not to reload.

For example, while face to face to an enemy, your main weapons ammo runs out. What do you think you need to do?
You use your pistol/secondary gun. It ain't there for fun.

When out of ammo, switch to your pistol and blast that guy to kingdom-come!

Notice, try your best to not reload in the middle of the road, or go on forwards where an enemy may randomly pop up.
Find a safe place to do it. Even stop if necessary.


Tip 6: Spawn Shields

Spawn shields pop up when you die. There main use for protecting you from an enemy who's taking advantage of your spawn placement.

With the spawn shield, you can do a Kamikaze without dying (If you get the timing correct.).
Also, if your grenade explodes, if you shoot or use your melee weapon, your spawn shield shall disappear..

Also,
Note that when you die the respawn time (Not shield.) lasts 5 seconds, and 3 seconds on a premium account.


Intermediate Tip: Clicking

Now, with most FPS, this has this thing:

You don't press...er...click and hold the shoot button (Left Click).

You keep on clicking. Basically "spamming" your finger on it.
Doing it this way shall give you less recoil and more accuracy.

And also, while shooting. Make sure the target is down. And when he/she is, stop shooting.
-Advised by Timcampy

Intermediate Tip: Opportunity

Always look for the best opportunity.

When your enemy's back is turned, shoot him' and take him out immediately.

Just take out him first if anyone else is around. No other enemy matters until you kill him.
-Advised by AznDragonX


Intermediate Tip: Sniping, and after Sniping

Move after every sniper shot.

Shoot and hide, and run for cover. Never stand still while shooting. Since you will be an easy target.

Switch weapons after every shot for a faster fire rate.
(Like: Shoot -> Switch to Pistol-> Switch to Sniper Back)

Scroll the mouse wheel down then up to switch weapons fast.
-Advised by AznDragonX

::CHAPTER TWO: AVOIDING SHOTS::

Tip 1: Move/ "Dance"

In any FPS game, you will have to come face-to-face to your enemy.

He/She's going to want to press the trigger as much you would want to too.

And in the end, you will at the same time.

In-game, you must take as much less deaths, and damage.

In order to not or to take as minimum damage as possible, do this:

A, Aim for the person who's after you, don't switch targets if you can beat him. Note that a Love Kill can beat a Sacrifice kill.
Since it may lead up to a Double kill.

--NOTE: Love Kills are Kills that happen when both players kill each other the same time, as for Sacrifice Kills, don't get confused with Kamikaze's.
Sacrifice Kills are obtained by shooting another enemy and killing them, while knowing an enemy is shooting you and you have no escape.

B, Shoot the enemy, while He/She is shooting at you, move and jump side to side. However don't always keep the same Left-Right-Left-Right Tempo.
Switch to diagonal movement, forwards or backwards. --What ever it takes to beat your enemy without barely any damage or any deaths.

Tip 2: In trouble!?

When out-numbered /ambushed, you know Grenades might not always be the best idea, directly.
Sometimes, it's OK to retreat. Fall back.

Take the route that'll most confuse the enemy, many twists and turns if possible. Sometimes use your Allies spawn shield.

As for being ambushed in the enemy spawn... you know not much anything good will happen if you get stuck in a corner.

Intermediate Tip: Suicide Bomb

Sometimes, you have to accept it that your dead. Funny I know.

But, heres a tip: Don't go out, without a bang! Be a sun!

When your ambushed, and no chance of survival, Pull out that grenade, hold it till it goes boom!
But of course, do this while next to an enemy or group of enemies.
-Advised by AznDragonX

::CHAPTER 3: STEALTH::

Tip 1: The Basics

You know James Bond doesn't go and say "Hey guys! Whassup?".

Solid Snake doesn't sneak to find candy either.

In stealth, you must remain as silent and unnoticed as possible. If thats your goal.

In stealth, there should be a point, mission, first of all.

Are you planning a sneak attack on a sniper?
Trying to sneak out with the flag?
Or are you going to plant a bomb where no one would notice, nor catch you on the job?

In stealth, pick the most unused route in the game. (Sometimes with your Allies if your planning an ambush.)

Remain silent. Even if you see the enemy, doesn't mean he/she sees you. Neither should they...

If you see an enemy, if your plan is to kill someone special, then killing, or should I say attacking someone else while you don't have their attention isn't and
shouldn't be a idea. (Under regular circumstances.)

Avoid unnecessary combat.

Only kill if you have been discovered, or such.

Also, I'm going to mention this again, the SHIFT key not only perks up your aim, but also makes you have no footstep sounds!

Tip 2: Time

Sometimes you have to finish your mission as soon as possible.
Take the short cuts, tell your allies to stall your enemies, something.

At times, you need to finish the mission. As good, as possible.
Sometimes you need to take use of your time, and maintain effective till it ends.

Intermediate Tip: Taking out an enemy

Heres a scenario for an example.
You're going along, sneaking in, and your job is to surprise enemies. Even if it's suicide in the end.

Going along, then, you spot a sniper, not moving. Just aiming at your allies.

Time for an Surprise attack!

This moment, you must not get the attention of anyone else, nor must you get the attention of the sniper. Don't Forget about the SHIFT key's extra ability. No sound from footsteps!

Take this Sniper out in this Scenario, but heres the point.

If your mission there requires you to be loaded, try melee-ing, or get a headshot with your pistol against the sniper. He can't see you, and you're right behind him.

::CHAPTER 4: SIDE TIPS::

Tip: The Weapon for you!

Know that there can't be a "most best weapon" anywhere.

Everyone has different masteries with weapons, some rather Machine guns, some Snipers.

Experiment and find the perfect weapon for you.

But of course, watch your wallet.


Tip: Servers

Play on the server which handles your country. Otherwise, playing on the EU Server when you live in the US will give you lag.
Lag is bad for gaming as you will play with difficult circumstances and not only you, but the other players will have a hard time playing with, or against you.
-Advised by Kenmoor

Tip: Co-operation!

In all team game modes, you have several other people fighting alongside you, most of the time. Take advantage of them! Aid each other!

Use the team-chat (Voice commands originally assigned as Z, X, and C. And Team Chat as F3.) to discuss tactics with your team-members to out-smart, out-number, and out-gun your opponents!

For example;

In CTF, you can tell your friends where you are if you have the flag, and where they should attack so that you can get to their base easier.

In Defusion, you can talk about who attacks/defends which bomb site, and where the other team seems to be focusing on attacking/defending.

In Build and Destroy, you can discuss structure-building tactics, and who does what.

In Defense, you can figure out where the best places to be to kill the bees are, and you can tell your team-mates where the enemy seem to be so that you can kill them off and secure the bees for yourself.

Even in Team Deathmatch, you can travel in groups, note enemy camping places, and tell your team-mates where the enemy is focusing on or attacking. By doing this, you can get an advantage in almost every situation.
-Advised by quicklite

::CHAPTER 5: ECONOMY::


Tip 1: Currencies

There are three different currencies in-game.

Force Points Points: Regular Points earned by battles. Used to buy Weapons/Items Directly

Brick Points: Earned by map downloads. (You can set a price to your map while registering it.) Used for the Treasure chest.

Tokens: Bought with real life money. Note that Everything costs the 1/4 - 1/5 rate of the price on items bought with Force Points points.

Tip 2: YOUR Economy

A guy buys a total of stuff that costs 1,600 Force Points points for example.

In order to raise or balance your economy, you must earn, as much, or more than you spend.

Remember this motto: "Earn more, than you spend."

If you don't you will slowly drain your money and end up with money that'll get you nothing. (Or nothing you personally don't need.)


Tip 3: Planning Purchases

When you going to buy a weapon for example, how long are you going to have it for? How long are you going to play today?

Sometimes you just need to think before buying. (You always have to.)
Buying a 7-Day Item wouldn't make sense if your just going to play for Five minutes.

In short, get what you need for the day, or remaining time. Sometimes don't get anything. But that is your choice!

::CHAPTER 6: MOVEMENT::


Tip 1: Speed

Did you think your pistol and your grenade use was just for battle?
Well it wasn't!

From any type of weapons, the Pistol and Grenade gives you more speed, due to it having maximum mobility.

So when your in a rush, you know you just have to pull out that Pistol. Or Grenade, what ever you'd like.
Although not as fast as the "Warpies" (Action Panel Item that gives you more speed.), it's as useful and efficient, also free.

Tip 2: Traversing

Climbing, leaping, anything to get to the other side, dodge the bullet, avoid the hole. Anything.

Know that a character in Brick-Force can jump 1.5~1.75 Blocks high. And about 2.3 Blocks forwards. Note that jumps don't alter/change speed, it can even make you slow sometimes.

Also if there is just a one block wide hole (1 x 1), you should know that you don't even have to jump in order to pass over it. So don't waste you time and speed jumping, just walk over it.

Intermediate Tip: Teamwork

When trying to get to the top, you always need a hand, or a head.

In Brick-Force, characters can jump on both enemies and teammates heads.
When trying to reach a tough place to get onto, that's where your team comes in.

You can use each other to get up to heights that you'd normally would never reach. Note that if theres even more then two people, there still has to be one guy who has to stay down.

You can use this to reach hidden routes, plant a bomb where players would even guess (The top?) , nor reach normally. Why not even surprise the enemy this way?

Intermediate Tip: Defusion Mode

Never go for the same bomb spot.
Make sure to vary in which one you go for, as well as the route you take to get there, or the other team will just see you coming, wait for you, and kill you.
-Advised by quicklite

Intermediate Tip: CTF (Capture the flag) Mode

For CTF; When you have the flag, there's no need to hurry!

Nobody knows where you are, and until you are killed or score, there is no way that the enemy team can score points.

Be stealthy!

Hide behind cover, take different routes, avoid the enemy until it is impossible to do so anymore.

Get as close to the flag point as possible before having risking being wounded or killed in an engagement.
-Advised by quicklite

Intermediate Tip: Deathmatch Mode

Don't stay in one place for too long!

Everyone's an enemy here, so if you stay put, there's only a matter of time before someone stumbles upon you and ends up killing you.

Be aware of the spawn points, as if someone spawns on or behind you, this is usually a death sentence.

Instead, use the abundance of hostiles to your advantage: As long as you can keep moving and use the mentioned in the previous chapters (Note, Chapter 1, 2 and 3), there will be many different targets to shoot at, and you can continuously rack up kills and win!
-Advised by quicklite

zazzer is putting together a Brick-By-Brick video with some amazing Tips & Tricks for Brick-Force.

Here is a list of a few I like to use.

Know your map. Know the exits and entrances into your base. And on

average how fast people can get to the main areas of contact.

KNow where the choke points are so that you can get multiple kills with a

single grenade. Avoid going into the choke points yourself so you don't

become grenade fodder.

Check both ways before crossing the street. Make sure you don't get shot

in the back. This is why it's better to check the other side that you

intend to go.

Use warpies so that you are harder to hit, and you have the speed to

circle around the enemy while he/she is trying to shoot you.

It's a lot easier to make a person run out of ammo shooting at you. Make

the enemy waste their ammo by only showing them your location, and when

they are reloading go for the kill.

Try to estimate where the enemy is by throwing a grenade into the first

POC is "point of contact". This way you can see if you wound someone by

seeing their health bars, which last about 3 seconds. So now you know

where the enemy is moving to.

Stay behind cover, whether it's a corner of a building, crates, or fellow

teamates. It's always best to have some sort of a shield, even if it's a

team member. Meat shields work too. Pop out from behind a corner just

quick enough to see an enemy. Most likely they will shoot at you and

waste their ammo. Listen for them to reload, then go in for the kill.

If you want to be a grenade ninja like me, practice cooking your grenade

so that it explodes JUST before you turn the corner to finish off the

enemy.

When you know an enemy is planting a bomb in difusion, throw a grenade

towards the bomb site. Even if you don't hit the person, the majority of

the people wills top planting and prepare for battle. This buys your team

some more time to kill the bomb planter.

Bursting your fire is a lot more accurate at longer ranges than holding

the trigger down and relying on spray and pray.

Aim for the neck or head for a quicker kill. Remember all guns have

recoil. So the more you shoot, the higher the bullets rise. If you aim

for teh feet it take smuch longer to get more damage dealt, than if you

would aim from the neck to the head. Total facial!

When you are in close range combat with an enemy, circle around them,

people have a hard time aiming at a person who is circling around them.

Always try to get behind the enemy, they never seem to expect the "sneak

attack". Most peopel are tend to worry about getting that kill, than they

are about staying alive for some reason.

Don't stand still like a dummy when in a gun fight, move side to side, or

in a circular pattern around your enemy. A moving target is always harder

to hit.

Brick-Force gives you multiple weapons, You are not just stuck using your

main weapon. When you are in close combat with an enemy, and you run out

of aammo, switch to your pistol to finish the kill. It's faster to switch

weapons than it is to reload your main weapon.

Don't always stay in the same areas, this isolates yourself and makes you

an easy target after the enemy you killed respawns. He knows where you

like to stay, and then can usually work their way behind you to get a

sneak attack.

Choose your weapons according to the maps. There's no sense to have a

sniper rifle on a small map. Choose accordingly.

I fyou want some fast kills and are not afraid to get killed. try and

stay around the enemy spawning site. Or stay around the bomb sites, or

flag site.

When you go up and down ladders, check all around the area you are about

to enter before you enter it. Nothing sucks worse than going up a long

ladder and getting shot in the back. Remember you can shoot when you are

on a ladder.

You ca actually hurd people into the direction you want them to go by

throwing grenades in front of them. You don't always have to get a kill

with a grenade. Yo can use them to control your enemies.

What are repairs?

Repairs are required to keep weapons at their peak performance. A well-working weapon is one of the key factors in winning a battle. A weapon that is damaged will only deal 50% of it's normal amount of damage in battle.

How do repairs work?

Repairing a weapon is simple. In the "My Items" section, click on the weapon you wish to repair. When a permanent weapon's durability reaches the point where a repair is of vital importance, a repair icon (A hammer) will be seen over the weapon. Click the repair option in the bottom menu and pay the required Force Points needed to repair the weapon.

As far as the specifics we have an example. Weapons decay by 0.5% each minute, which costs 10 FP to repair. A match lasting 10 minutes means a decay of 5% and a repair cost of 100 Force Points.
This means weapons can cost a maximum of 2000 FP to repair. Only weapons taken out for use during a battle will decay.

Why are repairs important?

Repairing a weapon will keep it at peak performance. A weapon with 0 durability will only deal half the damage normally dealt.

title: Why the B1 is the preferred light weapon of choice

posts.h:
Okay, so light weapons can debate-ably be the best type of weapon in the game. They can deal out of the most damage so long as the range is close, which is why they are usually the most favoured type of weapon on well balanced maps. The majority of the community who can afford whatever they want (excluding 5 star token weapons) usually lean towards the B1 also know as the Mosquito 1.

But why is this? What does this gun possess over it's almost equal counterpart the Scorpion 5? Well, the stats say they are basically equal for the most part, except with a few trade offs. So why is the B1 the preferred weapon of choice is the asked question again. I used to think it was the Band Wagon Effect. That being someone uses the B1 and pwns some newbs with it, then those newbs tell themselves "I'll get that gun someday because it's so freakin' overpowered."

However this isn't really always the case why the B1 is picked over the Uzi. I've had a few debates with people who have used both guns, and even I myself have used both. But I was shocked to find out why most people prefer the B1 who tried both guns. They often gave reasons like "it's more accurate and has less recoil." But wait, that isn't really true is it? They both have the same recoil and accuracy. At least that's what I can determine, and the stats even say that as well.

So why do people think the B1 is better. Well, here is my conclusion. The B1 doesn't really have better accuracy or better recoil. It's just HOW people use the guns. My hypothesis is that the increased fire rate of the Uzi only makes it feel like a more inaccurate and highly recoil gun. People see that increased fire rate, and often at times when they are in a medium ranged shoot out they will hold the fire button which will give their shots less of a chance of hitting if they were holding the fire button with the Uzi. So they are then getting more hits on average with the B1 because of how they play, and it also does one more percent damage, how could these people not then come to the conclusion the B1 is better right?

I still don't stand by the opinion that the B1 is "better" exactly. If I'm right, that just makes it the easier gun to use. Simply put, the B1 is more forgiving then the Scorpion. Both having trade offs, like the B1 being better the further you are away from the target over the scorpion. And the scorpion being better the closer you are to your target. I prefer the Scorpion myself though.
posts.t: Why the B1 is the preferred light weapon of choice

posts.h: What gun is better fully upgraded B2 or B1?

It's pretty much a sidegrade. I can tell you why I prefer the B1 though.

The Uzi has inferior range - I don't like being out-ranged. Inferior damage, too, even if it's just -1. Plus, a pathetic ammo count of 100. I think the only other weapon to have so few bullets is the noob gun.

I also don't find the advantages it offers instead all that advantageous. The +2.5% movement speed bonus is only marginally faster, and the faster rate of fire... well. You shoot a bit faster, but it also exacerbates the recoil and bullet spread. (If you used elite gems to upgrade an SMG to +10 in everything except RoF, you'd probably get a monster where you could just hold down the trigger and spray people to death from across the room.)

Also, because of the "client knows best" networking approach, and the fact that you can never know how much damage someone will tank before dying, it also means you'll waste a lot of ammo on players who technically died like 50 bullets ago, but haven't fallen over yet because they don't feel like it.

So in summary, slightly better damage + range > slightly better RoF + mobility.

Well, that pretty much translates into the B1 doing better at a longer distance, like I said. The scorpion should still have the slight edge at a very close distance. I suppose with latancy though if the two people were tied in skill and armour and everything else the battle would still probably end up in a tie. But my point is with the scorpion it might be possible to kill that opponent at point blank range in one more shot. And he might get one less shot on you because of it, or he might even get one less brickshot on you because you move just that bit faster than the Mosquito.

That being said the scorpion can still fair pretty well at the longer distances, not as easy to use as the B1 though. Part of the problem why most people fail with using the gun at longer distances though is probably because most of them use it how they would use a B1. You wouldn't use a Bronto like it's a sniper rifle (although I have seen some people try), so why would you use a scorpion like it's a Mosquito?

So my assessment is the Scorpion can probably kill a milli-second faster when up close and personal. It might only have a very small chance of you taking a little bit less damage because of the mobility. The B1 can kill probably milli-second faster at a medium range since that fire rate won't do you any better, but the 1% damage might save you from using one shot rarely. The problem is just that people don't know how to handle the scorpion properly at that range so they believe that the B1 can kill almost twice as fast. Although technically speaking the fire rate doesn't actually handicap you down if you know how to use the gun at that distance. And at a long range the B1 beats the scorpion hands down (although both medium and long range gun are way more plausible than either of these guns at that distance).

At least that's how I look at it. I could see even from my point of view why you would prefer the B1. I consider the trade-offs about equal and maybe the weapon of choice comes down to which map you are playing. Just like how most players of a high skill level usually bring a sniper specifically for certain maps. But won't touch the sniper in most closed in maps.

The basic formula to of getting Force Points...is getting kills. At the end of every match, the counter compares the "average" of how many kills you got, how many deaths, and assists you used. For example: Playing fully on an 8 min. match and getting 50 kills and 4 deaths can grant you up to 600 Force Points. Getting for example 10 kills and 20 deaths will grant you sbout 200-300 FP depending on assists. Just concentrate on getting more kills than deaths to get Force Points.
*A great way of getting even more FP is by playing Defense Mode. On an a 20 min. fight, the average of FP you can get are 1200 (If you agree not to kill each other)

-If your premium party overall is unsatisfied, the game makes no money

Hey guys.

As I have been asked many times before, I have started creating videos to share my knowledge and experience in gameplay pertaining to Brick-Force by using my experience from this game and many others.

I have been a gamer for nearly 20 years and have been competetive for most of it.
I had started my competetive gaming since Quake 1 switching to Quake 2 & Quake 3. I have won several "Quakecons" being in 1st place twice and 2nd place once. I know someone I talked to about with this said why they couldn't be the same people because support would have picked up multi-accounting for the sharpshooter contest, but think about it for a moment. LemonPop is from the US, and so is Skeptical and Pearl.

He went inactive right around the time the sharpshooter contest ended, but he participated half way through it. Odd huh? Well, sudden he is active again when this new ESL contest shows up. Playing with Pearl in ESL games? What are the chances? Well Skeptical got a 10 year ban from ESL and so did Pearl. Same punishment? Maybe the same people?

Basically these seem like names someone would use if they were making an alt account.

The new items just released a few hours ago. It also has a 50 ammo clip and despite the stats saying accuracy is low, I found it to be rather high in natural accuracy. The downside to this gun is that is it just barely inferior to the hornet in almost all stats. And the gun has a high recoil threshold. Obviously it's weaker than a Big Bang, but stronger or tied with a regular Boomer. What really makes the nade interesting is that Enemies can't really dodge it. It travels fast and explodes on contact with anything. If you accidentally hit an enemy directly up close, no damage from the nade is done to you. Although best I can figure, this is just a glitch.

I have both as well. I prefer my big bangs because they are way more over-powered though. The snowball has a few problems. It can't reach a lot of spots that a normal lobbing grenade can. It also has collision detection issues. Any hostile dead body that isn't even close to it can set the nade off early.

There are other reasons I use the big bang over it. The big bang kills fully armoured foes in one nade if it gets off two hits on the player. Two hits only usually occur though when the target it running away from the big bang. So most people trying to escape my big bang end up dying because they were trying to run away or run through it. Another reason is lobbing, bouncing, and correctly cooking let's the area in which big bangs can reach be much larger than a straight flying snowball. It's the weapon to use against people who love cover. Not to mention you get 4 big bangs and only 2 snowballs. Which if you use a boomer refill means 8 big bangs compared to 4 snowballs.

Sure snowballs are nearly impossible to dodge, but the same could be said about the big bang if you cook your nade just right. And even if it's a direct hit, it won't do much against tanks like me and most of the people I play against. A quick guide to the in-game Weapon Panel

posts.h:
You might have noticed the new weapons panel that pops up when you spawn and wondered "Nice. But how does it work?". Well, follow these steps, and you'll know how!

Step 1. Go to 'My Items' and click on the cogs at the bottom left hand corner of your screen, as shown here.


Step 2. You'll see an empty action panel, and all your items. Click on the item you want, and it will hover on your cursor. Move it to the action panel you want, click again, and you will put it back on the action panel.


Step 3. If you have multiple items you want to put here, just repeat step 2 until you have filled up all the action panel spaces that you want to fill up (or simply all of them :P)


Step 4. Click 'Set' if you are happy with your choices and would like to save them. Want to remove a few? Just click on the one you want gone, and then click the 'reset' button.


Step 5. Play Mode time! When you join a game, before doing anything, press 'k', and you will be presented with an array of the options that you picked. Pick the one you want before the time runs out, and play on!


Hope this helps .

I've played a mixture of normal matches and XP maps in the month that I played Brick-Force, and after an entire MONTH, I've made less progress than I could have in other games in two weeks, despite the fact that I played way more than I should have. The reason this slow rate exists is NOT because you have to work for it; there are click-to-kill MMORPGs with faster xp/money gain rates than this game. It exists just to get you to buy tokens. After all, this entire arsenal of guns is sitting there, staring at your face, and you can't even get a second tier gun without playing for a whole week, and this is assuming you've got every single day of that week off. The normal rate just doesn't work with other people's schedules, but they still want to get the power that payers possess. Hence, we have XP maps. All you'd have to do to get rid of most of them is re-balance all the guns and fix gems, action panels, armor, EVERYTHING. Of course, Infernum has never given a response that wasn't total PR to an idea like this.

Believe it or not, but the company that does the Chinese Brick-Force is even more P2W for the most part. That is excluding the 100k you get to start off with. There are a lot of items that are completely token exclusive over there. They are as follows; the space building blocks(which are bought piece by piece), clan logos, big gems, and space weapons. Not to mention most of their 4 star weapons aren't permanent and cost as much as Infernum charges for the space 5 star weapons. And action panel items are not buy-able in pieces of 100 to make them cost more FP as well. But then again, less action panel items would help balance the game kinda.

To me: XP maps = Grinding just like in any other games.

But then I throw that reasoning out the window when I see one highly ranked player against 7 green stared newbies. And then they leave when I join because they saw my rank. Even though I suck at the game. Hard.

To me: XP maps = Grinding just like in any other games.

To me: XP maps = Grinding just because the game is currently unbalanced or because they lag on big maps.

title: Did some field testing on Luck.

posts.h:
Okay, so we are know about luck. Ever wondered just how useful this stat is though.

Well, first off before I can explain the luck stat I first need to go in-depth on a "lucky". Most people question whether this is useful or not. So first let me explain what a lucky is, and how it happens. I had previously thought a lucky only happens when you are shot in the direct center of the head. This is called a brick-shot. You can not get a lucky unless the other player hits you with a brick-shot. Head shots and body shots won't trigger a lucky. What a lucky does when it happens is reduce damage. How much you may ask? Well, a lucky reduces damage to a normal headshot. So my Viper did 116 with a brick-shot. And it does 76 with a head shot. If I get a brick-shot and my opponent gets a lucky the damage was 116 and is reduced to 76.

To sum this up, a lucky reduces almost 40% of the damage from a brick-shot. Now how often does a lucky happen? Well, My testing wasn't too extensive, but I'd say on average a lucky has about a 20% chance of happening. This was among 180 brickshots that the average for all the results were in between a 20% chance.

So now for the luck stat? What does it do. Well, I ran 90 brickshots with no luck what so ever, and 90 brick shots with 32% luck. The difference? Does it increase the effect of a lucky, or increase the chance of a lucky happening? Neither as far as I can tell. Having more luck does not make a lucky reduce more damage. And as far as I can tell, having more luck doesn't increase the chances of a lucky happening either.

Here are my results for when luckys occurred.

This was with my max luck possible.

30 brick-shots with 32% luck = 10 luckys
30 brick-shots with 32% luck = 3 luckys
30 brick-shots with 32% luck = 6 luckys
In total, 90 brick-shots with 32% luck = 19 luckys

And my tests with 0% luck are as follows.

30 brick-shots with 0% luck = 9 luckys
30 brick-shots with 0% luck = 6 luckys
30 brick-shots with 0% luck = 8 luckys
In total, 90 brick-shots with 0% luck = 26 luckys

Yep, albeit I pooled a rather small amount of test trials, luckys happened less when I had more luck. I could run through 1000 brick-shots and I'm betting the results would vary every single time, but my best guess is that with or without high luck a lucky will happen just as often. If luck has any influence on a lucky, it is minimal at best.

Which is why I came to the conclusion the luck stat appears to be next to useless. While luckys are actually useful, but not that useful. Luck doesn't seem to have any influence on luckys. Perhaps the luck stat does something else? Like influence the amount of damage you do or influence you getting a brick-shot on your opponent rather being used defensively. Perhaps the stat is just bugged and doesn't influence anything because a fault in the programming. Like how melee weapons didn't get increased damage when they were upgraded. Who knows. All I know is my lucky pig canteen will be collecting dust for a while now.

Oh, and thanks DrRaven for helping me test the luck stat in-game.

I was playing with GraveBear a while ago. He kept telling me how to get better at the game. The one thing that stood out was that I should rapidly click my mouse rather than holding it down. I then noticed that everyone was saying that it's better. So here's my question: How is going
CLICK CLICK CLICK CLICK CLICK CLICK CLICK CLICK CLICK CLICK CLICK CLICK CLICK CLICK CLICK CLICK CLICK
better than my basic idea of holding the mouse down!!???

HOW!!!!????

Well, "CLICK CLICK CLICK" helps you lower down your gun´s recoil(knockback) and get more shots directly at your enemy. Each gun has recoil, and whle the more time you hold your mouse, the more recoil your gun will have(your gun will start shooting upwards from your recoil, and it will be harder for you to maneuver your gun directly at your enemy, which will lead to your enemy killing you).

Basically, you wanna have the least recoil as possible so you can deal more damage to your enemy.
Less recoil = Better accuracy

title: How to Broadcast LIVE! Game Play on Twitch.TV

posts.h:
A lot fo people seem to want to broadcast their gameplay, but seem to have issues with doing so.

So here I will make a friendly and hopefully easy guide to The Easiest & Most Lag Free to do so.

First you need to create your Twitc.tv account by Signing Up.

Signup to Twitch.Tv

Then you need to download these propgrams.

Open Broadcast Software
Install this program with the default settings.

DxTory Install this program with the default settings. And make sure you run the license file. (Yes it's legit).

In order to get these to record Brick-Force in fullscreen, (since it's not like any other normal game) you will have to follow a few different setup prodecures.

Setting up Open Broadcast Software


1) Install and run Open Broadcast Software.
2) Click on the setting tab, and open settings.
3) Under "Encoding" use the same settings in the pic.


4) Under "Broadcast Settings" use the same settings in pic.


You will find your Play Patch/Stream Key Here. And clicking on "Show"

5) Under "Video " Select "custom" and input your desktop resolution. I tend to use "Resolution Downscale" at 2.75 to reduce in game lag and internet lag. I use "Bilinear" and make sure there is no check in "Disable Aero at startup". Like the pic


6) "Advanced" should look like this.


7) Right click in the "Scenes:" area and click "add scene"
8) Name your scene "Brick-Force"


9) Right click under "Sources:" and add-> "Video Capture Device". Name it DxTory


10) Setting should be the same as in my pic.
posts.t: How to Broadcast LIVE! Game Play on Twitch.TV

posts.h:
Now to setup DxTory

1) Install and run DxTory
2) Now click on "Ignore Settings..." Click the Add "+" and add Open Broadcast Sofware into it like in the pic.


3) Now make sure your settings are the same as these following pics.


Of Course creating your own file locations





4) Now with everything setup and saved. You can open Brick-Force, sign in, and "Alt-Tab" back to your desktop and your will notice that "Brick-Force" is now selected in DxTory.


5) Now go to Open Broadcast Software. Click on Start Streaming.
6) Now you can go back into Brick-Force and you will see Green numbers in teh corner of your screen.
7) Now you can start your Broadcasting by selecting the F9 Button to start/Stop your stream.

You should now be ablt to view your Twitch.tv broadcast site and see yourself play.


This may seem like a lot of work to setup and run, But it's actually very easy, and basically a one-time thing. And it's THE ONLY WAY, to record Brick-Force in fullscreen, with very little lag at all.

Keep in mind that when you alt-tab while recording your viewers will only see a black screen.
YOU SHOULD NOW BE ABLE TO WATCH YOUR GAME PLAY ONLINE!!!

title: How to win in Brick-Force without paying a dime!

posts.h:
Hey guys hiimisaak here telling you how to dominate the brickforce world without paying money!

choosing a map
First step when you first start you get a black widdow 40 and a defult grenade (nade) and a griffon38 (pistol) you also get a wrench. None of these weapons are good so play a lot to get fp. Always play in Beginer server and I suggest playing in maps you are use to and is small (I like sky garden the most). Once you are level 21 and go into the FUN server I ask you politely to not any xp maps, even though you might want to many people will not like you doing this and may call you noob and or bad words. If you ever get bored of tdm (team death match) or ctf (capture the flag) try playig with your clan a b&d match (build and destroy) and a fun game mode everyone loves is defusion. I also suggest you play with a group of people you know that is at your level most of the time this makes it more fun and you wont get over powered buy pros.

Buying a good gun:
If you want to know what to buy you have to know the best guns that you cam buy with fp. Main:Locust,spider,mosquito,lightning,orion,spray watergun,watergun,piggy gun,pumpkin gun. Pistolselta,rubber ducky,buzzard. Melee:Princesswand,sword. Specialsosinons bomb,water baloon,blackpowder bomb. Now that you know what your goal is for buying guns you have to learn what guns to buy beofre you buy those weapons. I suggest getting the wasp first dont underestimate it even thought it is 1 star it is better then all of the 1-2 star weapons unless you are a amazing sniper. I would only buy a sniper if you have expirence in sniping from another computer game because the adder 69 is not that good. Snipers are the best weapons in the game though but only when you get the good ones. I also suggest you buy the harrier 33 for your secondary. Because of the low prices both of these guns are very good. Dont buy a melee or grenade until you buy at least a 4 star one the rest are worthless compared to the defult grenade. Then once you get enough fp I suggest buying the scaraba 4.16 and the buzzard 08 scaraba is a amazing gun for its price and the buzzard is very good with its very high accuracy. I also suggest that you buy your first new grenade the black powder grenade this is a great grenade for fp users. You can also choose to buy the soccerers wand but only if you have the FP because that isnt as important. Now I suggest you buy a main 5 star weapon if you ever got a aniper in the pick and win and thought you liked it I suggest you save and buy the viper or snake if you like the machine guns buy the locust or spider and for secondary the delta is the way to go if you happen to be on with a special offer buy the ducky gun. And for grenades buy the poisonous bomb.

strategy:If you want to be good at brickforce you are going to need a lot more then good guns your going to have to know how to aim qs how to doge and many other things. First thing you need to know is set your controls the way you are use to for sniping I use q because im use to not using left click. The best way to doge is going around someone while you are jumping kinda like you are making a circle around them while you shoot. For some reason this will work many times. For long distance shooting never hold while you shoot. If you are at least 20 bricks away from someone you just tap really quickly while you press your button that shoots. you can also help your aim by holding shift when you shoot this also makes you make no noise when you are walking but you do go bery slow. When you are sniping always be moving and I mean always! You never know when a sniper has his scope right on your head so dont make it easy for him (Or her)! Also turn your volume up for sound affects so you can hear people walking or shooting.

Armor
A huge part of this game is wearing and buying armor. The max armor you can have is 140, the way you get armor is buying accesories and upgrading them with upgrade gems. Brickforce use to have all season 1 accesories for fp but now only the green one is so you have to buy those. Once you buy them buy some upgrades. Always buy in the biggest stack you save a lot of fp with this. I suggest to not ever buy green gems because you can only upgrade your items 3 times then and that is not good or worth your money. I would start bying when you can get blue gems those you can upgrade to level 6 so they are way better.

other tips:
Try to hold a stash of money from 40-100k fp at all times because. Brickforce has a lot of special events that you can buy exclusive OP fp items. Often these items you can buy maxed and are usally 60k fp btu these special events usally only last about a day so always keep money. Also check all the brick by brick videos ( just look on brickforce web page or youtube it) they will help you a lot. Well thats it I hope that this helped!

Uhhh the guns that are tokens are still tokens. Most people still will buy tokens a ton + brickforce should make every weapon fp but have other stuff thats only tokens but doesnt affect how you build or how you play such as camo decals or clothing.
All the best guns are obtainable through FP so there's really little to no reason to even implement this idea. Most of the Flash Sales with rare weapons are also buyable with FP, albeit very pricey. If a gun is better, like the Snow Hornet, it's only better by 1-3% in terms of stats and make up for it by reduction in other stats (for more info. see "sidegrades"). There's not really anything game breaking.

The only reason for Tokens are vanity items and sped up progression by purchase of high-tiered guns earlier on in game, upgrade gems, and armor. If you want to go out in style, go buy tokens. I think that's a fair business model.

If anyone claims of a balancing problem, then the best solution would be to remove armor or reduce armor by a lot and as many people suggest, put a limit on nade spamming.

That said, by allowing FP to be converted into Tokens, you inadvertently promote farming of FP so you're going to see more XP/FP maps​. I don't know about you, but those maps make the game ultra boring.

Lastly, by implementing this, there would be less incentive to buy Tokens, hence less revenue. Think of yourself as a gaming company. Would you allow such a thing just to make a few people happy?

Wow, I am actually really surprised no one has mentioned the Orion Rare and the Snake Rare. Snake Rare is good for long range, its a one hit kill often. The Orion Rare is OP for all ranges, and even though its best for medium-long range, it works pretty well at short range too. Both guns have EXTREMELY good accuracy, but have lower ROF.

In my opinion there is no "best" weapon. Only solution to find out which is best for you is to play a little with a variety of weapons. Test different weapons and take notes which one you feel is right for your game play. Everyone has their own one weapon that they choose to use the most because they can manage to handle the strength of the weapon, but you shouldn't just depend on that one weapon to get you through. Switch weapons once in awhile and you'll get used to using different types of weapons no matter the speed or strength of it. Even if you feel that it's not strong enough, don't give up, practising with a weapon several times you will start to understand how to use that weapon and the positive or negative side on how to use it.

I think this game is pretty good, but I have some ideas to make it amazing. It has the potential to be great. This is listed in order of the importance of my ideas. Hope you consider them.

1. If players pay money on steam for the game, why make it pay to win? Winning should be based on skill, not money. To fix this, you should get rid of the store (except for clothes and accessories, but they should not have be able to be upgraded out of game.) and have a Counter Strike-like system where players earn points for doing things, such as getting kills (1 point), capturing flags (5 points), planting the bomb (5 points), defusing the bomb(5 points), and every time someone dies that is not the player in Zombie (3 per death), just to name a few. players can use points to buy better weapons like a really good weapon would cost like 30 points. Everything players bought and upgraded (including clothes. the clothes will stay but not the upgrades.) would only last the round, and get reset along with leftover points when the round ends. players also lose all their weapons when they die, but the points stay. 4. We need creatures. dangerous animals, aliens, monsters, and robots that all players have to watch out for. They should not be able to be used in Build and Destroy. But should be able to be placed down in making maps. you can also place down spawners with editable settings.

5.Ironsights!!!! do I need to say more?

6. Air control - When I have very low gravity I constantly fall off the map. It is because where players go while jumping is completely decided by what keys you press on the ground. having a little bit of air control would be very nice.

8. More weapons! more weapons could not hurt. my ideas: RPG(primary), C4(special) (can be placed on terrain, vehicles, other players, creatures, or if you want to be a living bomb, yourself. once the C4 has been planted the player who placed it is given a detonator. the C4 blows up when the detonator is used, or someone shoots it or blows it up. C4 is one use only.), dual glocks(secondary), desert eagle (secondary) Silenced weapons! that would increase the number of people trying to do stealth, but they don't have to use crossbows.

10. Make the voices less annoying! They extremely irritate me so either bring back the japanese voices or hire some real voice actors to talk normally!

11. I can not think of any more gamemodes, (maybe last man standing?) but more would be cool I guess.

Thank you for your time and I hope you take my suggestions into account. (especially the first one)

xXSpartanXx, oh those time we're quite an enemy and always came up with a 1 vs 1 sometimes I win and sometimes he would win. Even though I am level 40 and he is a higher and got stronger weapon then me I still win. Here is some tip.

.For heavy armor players, when you shoot the head instantly change to secondary and shoot at him again. Normally that would do the trick if you have a good sniper.
. When in the heat of combat, the enemy is most likely to aim at your face, so at some point crouch to avoid contact on the head and the uncrouch to avoid being slowed down. This is down in a matter of seconds.
. Get a better mouse
. Choose a sensitivity that is suitable for you, you can change your sensitivity in-game by pressing the key [ or ]
. When in a melee combat always try to go really close (and i mean really close) to him and go around him at the same time, this is unlikely possible but if successful then the result would be confusing your enemy and they have to move your mouse really fast in order to aim at you.
. Calculate your next move every time the enemy comes (e.g he throw a bomb at me i dashed to the left side, then quickly sidestep behind him and then melee him to death) and yes I did that xXspartanXx although he didn't die, I died

. title: BrackRoulette [Where Competitive Match Become the most Silly Match]

posts.h:
If You Ever Thought Competitive Match are Easy:
Then Try Playing another Competitive Match, with these Brackets!


BrackRoulette


What is BrackRoulette?
A: BrackRoulette is a gameplay where list of weird and unforgettable objective are given and you have to do what the given objective told you to do.

Isn't This Strat Roulette?
A: Yes, it is. You may face same strat from today's CS:GO's Strat Roulette but I also made new and different strat (or what I may say, "Brack").

Instructions
1.) Go to http://jklp.org/public/html/choose.html, it will lead you a website where you put random lines for random choice that will appear.
2.) The List of Bracks will appear below as you scroll down. You must copy and paste the whole list of Bracks to the empty box of the website.
3.) Once you had copy and paste the whole list to the empty box, click the button Choose and let the madness begins.

Requirements
  • 5 Clan Members (or alternatively 5 Friends)
  • All of the map that is officially made by Brick-Force, no custom maps
  • One Light Weapon, One Medium Weapon, One Sniper Weapon, One Heavy Machine Gun, and One Heavy Shotgun in your Weapon Switch Slots.
  • Any Secondary.
  • Any Melee.
  • Any Grenades. Smoke Grenade and Flash Bang are not allowed.
  • Skype, for better communication (Doing it with enemy and friendly will be weirder and stranger, but who knows.)
  • Headphones or Earphones.

Setting Up The Match with BrackRoulette
  • Choose any Defusion map that is made by Brick-Force: Dusty, Assault, Warehouse, Kill Hill, The Bridge, SniperHill, Terminal, Saraios, and WildWest.
  • Maximum of 10 players (5 vs 5 match)
  • Max round = 9
  • Drop must be ON
  • Mid-Game Joining must be ON
  • Game mode must be only Defusion
  • Prepare your BrackRoulette as I told you in the instructions above.
  • As the match start with all 5 friendly teams and 5 enemy teams ready for madness, do the first random chosen Brack (All players must follow one random Bracks per each round, Players can not do same Bracks and must do a different Bracks), then more Bracks until the game is over.

Have Fun, and remember: It's not about being so competitive, it's about having fun.

I would be very appreciated if anyone made a YouTube Lets Play whoever is doing BrackRoulette. German Language version will arrive soon. I just need someone who can translate the whole english word to german.

Feel free to create your own Brack and post them in private message to me so I can add them to the list, too!

Hello, Everyone! I'm Kagome0625, the Brother of Kagome0615 and I am here to help you and give you some facts and tips about Range, this can also be helpful for beginners as well.

So, What are range anyway and how do they work?
Range is the stat that can be found below Mobility at the stat and spec of the weapons of your desire. With the Range displayed, it will provide you the numbers of Brick the weapon's bullet can reach and travel. It is important to know what are the range numbers are in most weapons, so you can know how effective the weapon it is in distances.

How can we find Range in our Weapons?
The Range stat will be found in Main and Secondary weapons, the Close and Special weapons however does not provide the range. Given the fact that most Melee and Special weapons have their own throwing distances and how far it can reach to the target from distances, it still does not displays the Range for those two weapon category. But the Main and Secondary weapons is what makes it important.

What makes the Range important and why do I need to know about it?
Range are important because if you aren't paying attention of what Range does your weapon has, you aren't very sure or aware of how effective the weapon is in distances. So it is important to check and know what the Range of the weapon of your desire has and always either keep your distances or stay up close and personal.

We can know that:

  • Light Weapons has the shortest range than any other Main Weapon Category.
  • Medium Weapons has the longer range than Light Weapons'.
  • Long Weapons has the longest range than any other Main Weapon Category.
  • Heavy Weapons has the range between Light's and Medium's.

Regardless of what's the damage percentage, the accuracy, or the recoil of the weapons is, the Range can make some differences even though you have a different weapon that have either same damage, accuracy, etc. Most weapons are either equal or different to each other.

What is amazing that Range can make Medium weapons more accurate and devastating than Light Weapons because it has much more Range than the Light's. Meaning, if you have a Hurricane 4 and Mosquito 1 that both have same damage, but different Range, then Hurricane 4 will be the one that deals more damage because it has higher range than the Mosquito 1. Regardless of the same and identical damage and accuracy percentages.

The Higher the Range, The Higher the Damage Output in Distances.

So let's say that I have the Spider 36 that has the range of 40/125. What does 40 and 125 mean?
The first number before the bigger number are the distances of the block that can the weapon deal damage in its range. Meaning, that if your Spider 36 does 35% Damage, then it can deal the same damage (35% Damage) to a target from 0 to 40 blocks away from you. But, the bigger number (which is 125) will be determined and displayed for how far the bullet can reach and travel. If you're hitting the target from the range of 41 blocks to 125 blocks (as it passed the recommended firing range) the damage will decrease.

To clarify this:
Starting from 0 to 40 blocks: Still 35% Damage.
Starting from 41 to 125 blocks: Damage will slowly decrease dramatically from 34% to below.

But! If you the bullet reached or exceed the maximum range value, the bullet will then disappear or "despawn". Meaning, shooting at the enemy from 126 or more blocks away with the Spider 36 is futile and impossible to hit the target from that distances.

Are Range upgradable?
Apparently the Range of the Main and Secondary Weapon is not upgradable. However, if this stat is indeed upgradable, then it will become a devastating killing machine. Which is there is a good reasons why Range is permanently unable to be upgraded.

Watch the video to see Weapons with Range in Action to understand the facts and the usage of the Range.

Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nGjMH7kUiTQ



Well I hope that you have understand the usage and the facts about the Range. And tips for Beginners, don't forget that you can also crouch, can aim down most of the Weapon's Scope, and tap-fire your weapon by tapping your Left Mouse Button to make the accuracy and spread more focused and sharper so you won't miss the target and have nothing to worry about crosshair spread. And if you have any questions regarding about this tips and Range, feel free to write down and post it at this thread.

Good Luck!

title: Not Receiving Your Pick 'N' Win Coins?

posts.h:
Hello, Brick-Soldiers!

Ever have this strange feeling and realized that you're not receiving your Pick 'N' Win coin from your Continuous Play Reward? Do not worry! Sometime the Continuous Play Reward won't work properly as it used to be, but that doesn't mean it's permanently unresponsive!

When you see your Continuous Play Reward stuck at 1 minute and it has passed more than 2 minute, then it means that the Continuous Play Reward is not responding. But that is not the problem, in order to receive your Pick 'N' Win coins you must simply switch your current channel location into any different channel. For example: If you're currently at Beginner-1, then you must switch to any channel that isn't Beginner-1.

And do not worry that once you received your Pick 'N' Win coin by switching your current channel location to a different location, your Continuous Play Reward will not reset back to 70 minutes. Let us say that you have played for 100 minutes in Brick-Force (Every 70 minutes you will receive a Pick 'N' Win coin from the Continuous Play Reward,) then you switched a channel to receive your Pick 'N' Win coin in case your counter isn't working properly: Your counter will be set to 40 minutes, not back to 70 minutes again. Because the counter will remember how many minutes you have played in Brick-Force, so no need to worry about for playing another 70 minutes when you switch channel to receive your Pick 'N' Win Coin.

I hope that anyone (who is reading this and have their Continuous Play Reward not working properly) have understand and know how to receive your Pick 'N' Win coins!

See you guys at the battlefield and at the forum!
